clue.text: Film actress about to enter gala event

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so CA goes into BALL

blocks.note: a ball is a gala dance

explanation.surface: A film star arriving at a glittering gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Lauren Bacall, Hollywood star of the 1940s. The surface is exactly what she would be doing: turning up to a gala.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Lauren Bacall starred in To Have and Have Not and The Big Sleep opposite Humphrey Bogart.

clue.text: Second set of cards in haversack

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: A spare deck of cards stowed in a rucksack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' reads as an adjective, a second deck, but it is the verb: to second is to back.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a bag carried on the back: a backpack.

clue.text: Disable cold water movement

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
a ripple is a small movement on water

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch off a cold-water flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a plumbing or engineering order, disabling a cold water system; the definition is the verb at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to put out of action, as a strike might cripple an industry.

clue.text: Insect damaging to human life, initially

indicators.note: damaging something knocks it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
initially means at the start, so only the first letter of life is used

explanation.surface: A pest that threatens people's lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaging to human life' reads as one phrase describing a harmful bug, but 'damaging' is the anagram signal and 'to human' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the luna moth is a large pale-green North American moth, one kind of insect.

clue.text: Departure location’s pretentiousness before journey

indicators.note: before means placed ahead of, so AIRS comes first and TRIP follows

explanation.surface: Showing off before setting out on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway, the place a plane departs from, so a location for departures.

clue.text: I had top removed from concrete - perfect

indicators.note: in a down answer the top of a word is its first letter, so REAL loses its R

explanation.surface: A builder complaining that the top layer of concrete had been stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like the building material; here it is the adjective, real.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as adjectives both describe something that could not be better.

clue.text: Less than adequate discount, perhaps

blocks.note: a discount is a second, lower rate of price

explanation.surface: A shop discount that turns out to be stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, 'second rate' is what a discount gives you: a second price rate below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: mediocre work falls short of adequate, and a discounted price is literally a second rate.

clue.text: Line is buried in many sheets of paper? It shows what actually happens

indicators.note: what is buried lies inside something else, so L and IS go inside REAM

explanation.surface: A single line lost among a huge stack of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a whimsical definition: realism in art shows life as it actually is.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism in art and literature aims to show life as it truly is, not idealised.

clue.text: A plan involving an upset in American territory

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so A MAP takes AN inside it
upset means knocked over; in a down answer that turns the whole assembly upside down, reversing it

explanation.surface: A scheme that runs into trouble somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An upset' looks like a noun phrase, but 'upset' acts on the whole assembly, which is then read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Panama is a Central American country, a territory in the Americas.

clue.text: Reviewed one idea about power, like tragic king?

indicators.note: to review is to go over again and recast, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round P

explanation.surface: A critic reconsidering a play's central theme of power and a doomed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Oedipus is the tragic king of Sophocles' play; the question mark admits the adjective is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipean is the adjective from Oedipus, the Theban king of Greek tragedy who unknowingly killed his father.

clue.text: Patrons unexpectedly elect to retain right of possession

indicators.note: what happens unexpectedly departs from the expected order, so ELECT is rearranged
to retain is to hold on to, so the rearranged ELECT holds LIEN inside

blocks.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Voters electing to keep a property right.
explanation.walkthrough: LIEN is a legal term worth knowing: the right to hold someone's goods until they pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of customers of a business, the people who patronise it.

clue.text: Tea popular in a number of cafes, perhaps

blocks.note: cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A tea that is in favour at lots of cafes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a café scene, and the definition belongs to it: a set of cafés under one brand is a chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: cafes owned under one brand form a chain, like shops or hotels.

clue.text: Confusion about piano or wind instrument

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so PIE goes round P

blocks.note: pie is printers' slang for a jumble of type

explanation.surface: A muddle over whether to play piano or a wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE meaning confusion comes from printing, where spilt type is 'pied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the pipe, as in pipe and tabor, is a simple instrument played by blowing.

clue.text: Fellows suppressing wrong number, keeping one hidden for a long time

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down and keep it in, so MEN holds ILL inside
to keep is to hold, so NUM holds I inside it

blocks.note: num. is the abbreviation for number
I = one, the Roman numeral, which is the letter kept hidden

explanation.surface: Men covering up a wrong number and keeping a secret for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers in a row: M(ILL)EN then N(I)UM. 'Hidden' only describes the I tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A millennium is a thousand years, the idiomatic 'ages' of a long time.

clue.text: Fully prepared to study Irish poet, mostly covering time overseas at the outset

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so YEATS loses its last letter
to cover is to go over and enclose, so YEAT wraps round T and O
the outset is the start, so only the first letter of overseas is used

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
W B YEATS minus its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone well prepared to study a famous Irish poet after time abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'to' after the definition is only a link. The poet is W B Yeats, whose name loses its S before wrapping round the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-to-eat describes food sold already cooked, so fully prepared for the table.

clue.text: Top class deal arranged and maintained by country’s foremost soldiers, repeatedly

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so DEAL is rearranged
to be maintained is to be held up and supported, so the rearranged DEAL is held between the CREMEs
foremost means first, so only the first letter of country is used
repeatedly means more than once, so C + REME appears twice

blocks.note: REME = Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
the second copy of C + REME

explanation.surface: An elite arms deal handled by the nation's leading troops.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's corps of engineers; C + REME, twice, sandwiches the rearranged DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'cream of the cream', used in English for the very best, the elite.

clue.text: A practical scientist, perhaps, welcoming a US statesman?

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so A LAB MAN takes A inside

blocks.note: A + LAB MAN, one who works in a laboratory
used as is, going in after A LAB

explanation.surface: A laboratory scientist receiving an American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' is split as state's man: a man of a US state, here Alabama. The question mark flags the wordplay in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: a statesman read as state's man, a man from a US state, and an Alabaman is exactly that.

clue.text: Froth on drink? See male tucking in beam

indicators.note: on means on top of; in a down answer HEAD sits above the drink
to tuck in is to slip inside, so M goes into LAP

blocks.note: the head is the froth on a beer
to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Looking at the foam on a pint while a man tucks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Froth on drink' reads as one thing, a beer's head, but 'drink' is a separate verb, LAP, with the male tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition names the output for the object: a headlamp is what produces a car's beam.

clue.text: Editorial comment describing provocative questions - clear it needs editing

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so CLEAR IT is rewritten into a new order

blocks.note: leading questions push towards an answer

explanation.surface: An editor demanding a comment piece full of loaded questions be tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper setting runs through the whole clue, with 'editing' doing double duty as surface and anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leader, the article stating its own opinion, is its editorial comment.

clue.text: That, in archaic fashion, is linked to peer near the beginning

indicators.note: to be linked to something is to be joined on to it, so YON attaches after EARL

blocks.note: an earl is a British peer
yon is old English for that

explanation.surface: A remark on old-fashioned phrasing, with a nobleman somewhere at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads back to front: YON is named first but comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'early on' places something in the first part of a period, near its beginning.

clue.text: Indian bread apparently in discussion supported by India

indicators.note: in means inside, so AP goes inside CHAT
what is supported rests on something; in a down answer I sits underneath

blocks.note: ap. is an abbreviation of apparent(ly)
I = India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Indian bread seemingly being talked about, with India backing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' looks like a hedge in the surface; it is an abbreviation, AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the chapati is a flat unleavened bread from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Man, tense, embraced by man that’s near

indicators.note: to be embraced is to be held inside someone's arms, so T sits inside MISER

blocks.note: near means stingy, so a near man is a miser

explanation.surface: A man held close by a man standing nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is the old sense stingy, not close by; a man that's near is a MISER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mister is the title given to any man, and in speech ('Hey, mister') it stands for the man himself.

clue.text: Absurd rail works receiving allocated quantity

indicators.note: to work something is to knead it into a new shape, so RAIL is rearranged
to receive is to take in, so the rearranged RAIL takes RATION inside

blocks.note: a ration is an allocated amount

explanation.surface: Complaint about pointless engineering works on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail works' looks like maintenance on the line; 'works' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something that defies reason or logic.

clue.text: Something not wanted soaring round one’s head

indicators.note: soaring means rising; in a down answer NONO is read upwards, reversing it
round means surrounding, so the reversed NONO goes round I

blocks.note: a no-no is something not allowed or wanted

explanation.surface: Something unwelcome flying round a person's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off one's onion' is British slang for mad, where onion means head. 'One's head' looks like one phrase; the 's joins I to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang sense: 'off your onion' means off your head, so onion is the head.

clue.text: Worker ate about noon

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so HAD goes round N

explanation.surface: A labourer eating at around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a lunch break; 'Worker' is the definition, as in a farm hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand as a hired worker survives in farmhand, deckhand and 'all hands on deck'.

clue.text: See 3
Flavoursome plant in the Bible for you and me

blocks.note: thy is the old biblical form of your

explanation.surface: A herb mentioned in the Bible, shared between us.
explanation.walkthrough: THY is the King James Bible's word for 'your', so the Bible's word for you(r) plus ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: thyme is a herb grown for its aromatic, flavouring leaves.

clue.text: One loved working of animator around end of Cinderella

indicators.note: working something means kneading it into a new shape, so ANIMATOR is rearranged
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round A
the end of a word is its last letter, so Cinderella gives A

explanation.surface: An animator's beloved work on the finale of Cinderella.
explanation.walkthrough: The Disney setting is decoration; the definition is 'One loved', a female beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for a female sweetheart, borrowed into English for a woman who is loved.

clue.text: Sound of phone ultimately jarring during start of religious chant

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of jarring is used
during means in the middle of, so G goes inside INTONE
the start of a word is its first letter, so religious gives R

explanation.surface: A phone going off loudly in the middle of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Every church-goer knows the scene; the definition sits at the start, and 'religious chant' splits into R and INTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringtone is the tune or tone a mobile plays to announce an incoming call.

clue.text: Apparently weak figure having quiet power around border

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so SH and P go round RIM

blocks.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A seemingly feeble person who quietly holds power along a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' hedges the definition: a shrimp is a small, puny-looking person who may yet have hidden power.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: calling someone a shrimp mocks them as small and puny, the look the clue hedges with 'apparently'.
